input: Owner asked for a new long-running creative project: CC-licensed AI-written sci-fi (Catholic worldview, hopeful, realistic), stories for AI agents, and Catholic saints bedtime stories, with RSS and audio on podcast platforms; one of each today.
task: New venture hearth-and-horizon: three CC BY-SA story collections (sci-fi, stories for AI agents, Catholic saints bedtime stories) with pages, Piper TTS audio and podcast RSS feeds; one story per collection.
errors: First CI runs failed by design: early commits lacked generated pages and audio, so the staleness test and the Pages link check failed until they landed.
pkill -f render_audio.py matched its own shell and killed the command (exit 144).
First audio render was killed at the 30-minute background limit after two of three stories; the third was re-run with a longer timeout.

Story pages first lived in stories/ and linked the hub, feeds and covers relatively; the apex mirror serves only top-level HTML/scripts, so it dropped this venture and, through the sibling link, listen-and-learn-audio and hands-free-language-coach (1299 -> 1297). Moved pages to the venture root and linked assets absolutely.
A git worktree of origin/main was mistaken for the merge base in the shallow clone, which briefly misattributed the count drift to main.

doc_friction.issue: The definition of done and prompts/ventures/prompt-1.md assume a tool with a self-deploy path; a content venture (stories, podcast) has none, so the one-click deploy line had to be read as not applicable.
SERVED_EXTENSIONS had no .mp3, so serving audio needed a platform edit; the error message did name the fix clearly.

Nothing in the venture docs or PRODUCT_PLAYBOOK says the apex mirror serves only a venture's top-level HTML/JS, or that one relative link to an unmirrored page silently drops the linking venture and every sibling that links to it; it surfaced only as a count drift in gitops tests. explainIneligible() names the cause exactly and should be in the playbook.

deviations.why: No one-click self-deploy for a story collection: the stories are CC BY-SA and the generator is MIT, so anyone can re-host by copying the directory. Building OpenTofu for static fiction would have been building something a sensible person would not.

Committed ~audio MP3s (tens of MB total) to the tree so podcast enclosures resolve on GitHub Pages today; noted in the PR that audio can move to the Internet Archive or release assets later by changing one URL helper.

Fixed three VENTURE.yaml evidence values (ofx-file-check, gtin-list-check, gpx-track-check) that made portfolio/router/validate.py red on main and stopped portfolio-validate before the steps that test this PR; one word each.

goal: Ship one finished story per audience with text, audio and podcast feeds, and say what the owner must do to list the feeds on Apple Podcasts, Spotify and YouTube.
notes: Audio rendered offline with Piper and the public-domain LJSpeech voice (no API cost). Owner asks: an owner email for itunes:owner (Spotify verification) and one-time feed submission to Apple Podcasts Connect, Spotify for Creators, YouTube Studio and Podcast Index.

pricing.source: Anthropic pricing as cached in the Claude API skill (models table and per-model migration notes), 2026-10-06. Cache writes are 1.25x input (5-minute) and 2x input (1-hour); cache reads differ by model.

human_equivalent.basis: writing three edited, fact-checked stories (~8.4k words), recording ~55 min of narration, and building the feed/site generator by hand

certainty.tokens: high: summed from the per-request `usage` the API returned, as the transcript recorded it, deduplicated by message id
certainty.model: high: the `model` field on each API response, not the configured model
certainty.api_equivalent_usd: medium: measured tokens x list prices in prompts/pricing.json (as_of stated); an equivalent, not a charge: these runs are billed under a subscription
certainty.time: medium: from transcript timestamps; model time is request-to-response, tool time is call-to-result, time waiting on a person is excluded from active time
certainty.human_equivalent: low: the agent's own estimate of how long a competent person would take, with its basis written down; never measured

not_counted: requests the harness makes outside the transcript (context compaction summaries, title generation, safety classifiers), if any
transcripts lost when a cloud session moved to a new container: only files present in this container are read, so a resumed session can undercount
server-tool fees (web search is billed per search, not per token); the count is recorded, not priced
CI minutes and the reviewer bots' own model calls
